solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seed-spiller nailed by stop-motion animation

indicators.note: the answer is held fast, as if nailed, inside the run of letters in stop-motion animation

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of the words motion and animation

explanation.surface: A biblical figure gets skewered in a claymation short.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Onan spilled his seed on the ground rather than father a child for his dead brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical character is remembered chiefly for wasting his semen, hence the term onanism.

clue.text: Of inwardly malleable shape

indicators.note: only the inner letters of the word for shape are pliable, so the two middle ones get reshaped while the ends stay put

parts.note: form as a noun is the outline or configuration of something

explanation.surface: A description of something whose shape can be moulded from within.
explanation.definitionFit: Both prepositions can mark the material something is made with: a ring of gold, a ring from gold.

clue.text: Retainer lifted bloody thing in birdcage

parts.note: a retainer is a fee paid in advance to secure a lawyer's services

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word means reading it upwards, so it runs backwards

parts.note: blood is red, so bloody gives the colour

explanation.surface: A servant hoisted something gory into a bird's cage.
explanation.walkthrough: Retainer looks like a servant, but it is the payment to a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed or water dispenser clipped to the bars of a cage is a standard piece of bird-keeping kit.

clue.text: Octets ready for old Don?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ready is slang for cash, and a Don is a Spanish gentleman, so this is old Spanish money

explanation.walkthrough: The old Spanish silver dollar was worth eight reales, hence its English name; the phrase is the parrot's cry in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means groups of eight; historically it names the Spanish dollar coin.

clue.text: A prisoner parts with a snake

indicators.note: the convict separates the two halves of the other phrase, splitting it to sit between them

parts.note: and means with, plus the a as written
taken as written
con is short for convict

explanation.surface: An inmate leaves, taking a snake with him.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts looks like a verb of leaving; here it means splitting something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant South American constrictor is one of the largest serpents in the world.

clue.text: Kid always safe given cake!

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, as in a peterman or safecracker
Chambers gives pan as an intransitive verb meaning to cake, to form a hard crust

explanation.surface: A child forever protected as long as there is cake to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is underworld slang for a safe; a safe-blower was a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's hero is the boy who never grows up, a child for ever.

clue.text: Troubles again for the ear with scented applications

definitions.note: the answer is singular, the turmoil of mortal life, while the clue word is plural

indicators.note: what is heard rather than seen, so the letters only need to sound like the word for again

parts.note: more, as in once more
talc and oil are both perfumed things applied to the skin

explanation.surface: Fresh worries about ear drops and perfumed lotions.
explanation.walkthrough: Coil in Hamlet's 'shuffled off this mortal coil' means turmoil, the bother of living.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for the cares and tumult of human life, so it fits worries or turmoil.

clue.text: Novel eulogy for 27 23?

definitions.meaning: the answer is the title of an H. G. Wells novel
27 and 23 make dead parrot; a eulogy recounts the life of the deceased, and Polly is a stock name for a parrot

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give DEAD PARROT, the Monty Python sketch; a life story of a dead parrot called Polly is the Wells title.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells's 1910 comic novel tells the life of a draper's assistant, which doubles as a memorial account of a parrot.

clue.text: Edvard is probably wearing no pants

indicators.note: pants as a British slang adjective means rubbish, so the letters are badly done and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter caught out without his underwear on.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like trousers or underwear; in British slang it means rubbish, flagging a jumble. Edvard Munch and Edvard Grieg were both from Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A man called Edvard, spelt that way, is likely from Norway, like the painter Munch or composer Grieg.

clue.text: Carry on the wrong way with hot date

indicators.note: the word for carry on is read in the wrong direction, backwards

parts.note: to cope is to carry on, to manage

explanation.surface: Behaving badly on a steamy romantic evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry on suggests misbehaving; here it means cope.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch can be the fixed point in time from which a period is reckoned, a date in that sense.

clue.text: CID man ill-prepared for showers, it seems unsettled

parts.note: someone caught in the rain without a mackintosh has no mac
a Detective Inspector works in the Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: A detective unready for the rain seems out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: CID MAN is one letter short of an anagram of the answer, a deliberate decoy; a mac is a British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples move from place to place with no fixed home, so they are unsettled.

clue.text: The suffering with each cat

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, damaged and so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pain shared out with every feline.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal is a big spotted feline of Africa.

clue.text: Cape is comparable with cycling regalia

indicators.note: the phrase for comparable is rotated, its first part moving round to the end

parts.note: if something is comparable it is on a par

explanation.surface: A cyclist's cape stacks up against the rest of their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling suggests bike kit; it signals that ON A PAR IS becomes A PAR IS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental covering for a horse, and by extension rich trappings or finery.

clue.text: Was it opened by declaring Martin Luther a heretic?

definitions.meaning: the idiom of opening one to unleash a mass of trouble
Luther was condemned at the Diet of Worms in 1521, the German city

explanation.walkthrough: Worms is the German city where the imperial diet condemned Luther, a decision that let loose the Reformation's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a situation that causes many unforeseen problems once started, punning on the city.

clue.text: Quaker takes moments for Revelation

indicators.note: the Quaker's name takes in the word for moments, holding it inside

parts.note: William Penn, Quaker founder of Pennsylvania
time as in moments or a while
to as in heading for

explanation.surface: A Quaker spends a few moments on the Book of Revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: Revelation suggests the Bible's last book; here it is an art term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentimento is an earlier painted image showing through later paint, a reappearance of what the artist covered.

clue.text: Institutions that educated 23s, reportedly

indicators.note: as reported in speech, the letters only need to sound like the word for parrots

parts.note: 23 is PARROT, so these are parrots, often called Polly

explanation.surface: Colleges once taught people to repeat things, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: British polytechnics, known as polys, became universities in 1992, hence the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Polytechnics were further-education colleges in Britain, so they are institutions that taught.

clue.text: Sister university stops news letter to the Hebrews

definitions.meaning: the fourteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet

indicators.note: the university abbreviation plugs the gap between the two letters, stopping it up

parts.note: read as new plus s, two Ns, N being new

explanation.surface: A nun from a university blocks a newsletter to Jewish readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter to the Hebrews sounds like the epistle in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order, and nun is also a character in the Hebrew script.

clue.text: Fratricide engages suitable officer

indicators.note: Cain takes on the word for suitable, holding it within

parts.note: Chambers' first sense of fratricide is one who kills a brother; Cain killed Abel
apt means fitting

explanation.surface: A brother-killer recruits a fitting military man.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army and navy, and the commander of a ship.

clue.text: Lexicographer looks up dividing key group

indicators.note: the reversed name splits the word for key into two parts

parts.note: a cay or key is a low island or reef

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Peter Mark Roget compiled the thesaurus

explanation.surface: A wordsmith consults his references to sort a crucial set.
explanation.walkthrough: Looks up suggests consulting a dictionary; it signals reversal. A key in this sense is a small island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or division of things sharing characteristics, a group.

clue.text: Bones appear well established in X-rays?

indicators.note: the established word sits inside the word for pictures

parts.note: X-rays are pictures, pics
to root is to become firmly established

explanation.surface: The skeleton shows up clearly on the scans.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that X-rays are only one kind of picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Prootic bones are a pair of skull bones in front of the ear in fish and reptiles.

clue.text: Peace activist that's bad news in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word only needs to sound right

parts.note: oh no is the cry at bad news

explanation.surface: A pacifist warning a theatre audience of disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono campaigned for peace with John Lennon, notably the 1969 bed-ins.

clue.text: Fine threads, light with it?

parts.note: lint is fluff made of loose threads and fibres

explanation.surface: Tiny fibres you can strike a light with.
explanation.walkthrough: Flint struck against steel throws sparks, so you can make a light with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is the hard stone struck with steel to produce sparks for starting a fire.

clue.text: See 8
Overall that would initially be only a tenth as valuable

indicators.text: that would initially be only a tenth as
indicators.note: in Roman numerals C is a tenth of M, so swapping the first letter of the answer for C would cut its value to a tenth

parts.note: costly means expensive

explanation.surface: A garment worth only a tenth of the price.
explanation.walkthrough: Overall looks like a work garment; it is the adverb. Change the M (1000) at the start to C (100) and the answer becomes the word for valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall and mostly both mean on the whole, for the greater part.

clue.text: Repeat the usual nonsense

parts.note: par is the normal standard
rot means rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Trotting out the same old drivel again.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words mechanically, as the bird mimics speech.

clue.text: See 4
Was writing somehow discernible with line obscured?

definitions.note: the answer is a simple past tense, standing in for wrote

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other order
obscured says the letters of line are hidden away, removed from the mix

explanation.surface: Was the handwriting legible, with a line blacked out?
explanation.walkthrough: Take L, I, N and E out of DISCERNIBLE and rearrange the remaining DSCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribe is an old verb for to write, so its past tense matches putting words down.

clue.text: Low blow

explanation.walkthrough: Blow looks like a punch, and the pair suggests a low blow; it means spend recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sad is feeling down, and to splurge money is to spend it all in British slang.

clue.text: Utterly obsolete

definitions.meaning: second meaning: no longer in use

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single phrase; they are separate meanings, an adverb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it intensifies, completely; as an adjective it means defunct, as with a language no longer spoken.

clue.text: A little contretemps over measuring device

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the hidden run is read backwards
a little of a word is a short run of its letters

explanation.surface: A minor disagreement breaks out over a gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas or electricity gauge records how much has been used.

clue.text: Meetings pass with Louise and I conducting Q&A

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the name and I carry the question letter within them

parts.note: Lou is short for Louise
the Q of Q&A is taken as written and tucked inside the name and I
taken as written
the A of Q&A is taken as written and goes at the end

explanation.surface: A trip over the pass with two people running a question session.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquia are academic conferences or seminars, formal gatherings for discussion.
